newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas shares close higher as rally continues.
newsitem.headline: Caracas shares close higher as rally continues.

text.p: Share prices on the Caracas Stock Exchange edged to higher for the third successive session Thursday as investors anticipated a hike in electricity tariffs and foreign buyers showed confidence in the economy's recovery, brokers said.
According to preliminary figures from the exchange, the market's 19-share index rose 0.32 percent to 6,669.30.
Market leader Electricidad de Caracas, which routinely accounts for over half of total trade, continued its rally rising 6.50 bolivars to 536.50 bolivars.
Energy and Mines Minister Erwin Arrieta has said electricity tariffs are to be adjusted shortly although he warned Thursday that the rate increase would not match power companies' expectations.
"Definitely the strongest stock of the session was Electricidad due to the imminent rate adjustment," said Harold Cuellar of the Cavelba brokerage.
Another broker noted that the market was showing "support due to re-entry and interest which foreign investors are showing."
A total of 20 stocks rose, 17 fell and five closed flat in strong trade of 7.2 billion bolivars ($14.9 million).
The composite Merinvest index, which includes telephone company CANTV, rose 0.42 percent to 105.74.
CANTV slipped 11.00 bolivars to 2414.00 bolivars, steel company Sivensa rose 0.25 bolivar to 160.25 bolivars and leading bank Banco Provincial rose 19.95 bolivars to 889.95 bolivars.
